subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Gothic Cathedrals: Engineering Faith
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gothic Cathedrals: Engineering Faith.

hook.text: Notre-Dame's roof weighs 13,000 tons. Medieval builders raised it 33 meters without steel or cranes.

buildup.text: Gothic builders invented the flying buttress — external arches that push walls inward against wind.

discovery.text: Pointed arches distribute weight more efficiently than round ones, allowing thinner walls and bigger windows.

twist.text: Beauvais Cathedral aimed to be the tallest ever. Its vault collapsed twice. Ambition exceeded engineering.

climax.text: Cathedrals took over 100 years to finish. Workers never saw the completed building in their lifetimes.

punchline.text: They built for God. They engineered for gravity.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a flying buttress in Gothic architecture?
options: It decorates the exterior with ornamental arches
It pushes walls inward to resist outward forces
It channels rainwater away from the foundation
